conclusions: The truncated second moment over the open upper tail satisfies ∫_{(t,∞)} x² dμ(x) = [t/sqrt(2π)] exp(-t²/2) + μ([t,∞)), where μ is LocalDef001 and the tail mass is converted to Real.
The same truncated second moment satisfies ∫_{(t,∞)} x² dμ(x) ≤ [(t+1/t)/sqrt(2π)] exp(-t²/2).
mathematical_definitions: Let μ = gaussianReal 0 1, a fixed nondegenerate Gaussian measure on the Borel real line.
The integral is the real Bochner integral of x ↦ x² with respect to μ restricted to the open interval (t,∞).
The term μ([t,∞)) in the displayed real identity means ENNReal.toReal applied to the μ-mass of the closed interval [t,∞).
The common exponential normalization factor is exp(-t²/2)/sqrt(2π).
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every real threshold t at least one, the Gaussian second moment above t equals a boundary-density term plus the closed upper-tail mass, and it is at most the same density factor multiplied by t+1/t.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The conclusion is restricted to thresholds t≥1, so in particular the reciprocal 1/t has a nonzero positive denominator.
The integral is over the strict tail x>t, while the measure term in the exact identity uses the closed tail x≥t.
The measure term is Measure.real, namely ENNReal.toReal of the set mass, rather than a literal ENNReal term.
The result concerns only the second moment x² and does not assert an analogous formula for other powers or functions.
The upper bound is one-sided and does not provide a matching lower bound or an asymptotic equivalence.
The fixed measure has parameters exactly zero and one; no statement is made for arbitrary Gaussian location or scale parameters.
No separate integrability or finiteness hypothesis is present; the target uses the total definitions of the integral and Measure.real.
The hypothesis is satisfiable, so the implication is not vacuous.
ambiguities: The dependency information identifies the second parameter of gaussianReal only as an NNReal parameter v and does not independently state whether it is conventionally called a variance, scale, or another Gaussian parameter.
The packet does not expand gaussianPDF, so the displayed factor exp(-t²/2)/sqrt(2π) is recognized from the target formula rather than derived from an exposed density definition.
The target itself does not state atomlessness at t, even though it combines an integral over (t,∞) with a measure term on [t,∞).
